title: Locker and Scholarship
premise: Wendell Blackwood has spent seventeen years in Millbrook making herself small, but when her best friend and secret crush, Priya Chandrasekaran, vanishes the night before the scholarship interview that was supposed to be their shared escape, Wendell finds Priya's keys and a trail of coded notes pointing toward a runaway network and Priya's controlling family. As Wendell searches, she's forced to ally with people she's spent years avoiding, come out on her own terms, and realize invisibility was a cage she built. The climax comes at a bus depot on the night of the state finals, where Wendell must choose between chasing her own scholarship future and standing publicly beside Priya; the book ends with the two of them staying—not rescued, but returned by choice—to rebuild Millbrook into a place worth staying in, together.
about_author: Xanthe Underhill is the pen name of a former small-town debate champion who now writes from a converted grain elevator in the Midwest. Their fiction centers quiet kids who discover that silence is a choice with a price.

chapters.title: The Combination
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A tour of Wendell's carefully managed invisibility: perfect grades, closed locker, one friend, Priya. Establishes the scholarship they've both been chasing as their shared exit plan. Emotional beat: the ache of wanting more while pretending not to.

chapters.title: Keys on the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Priya misses their study session, then misses school. Wendell finds Priya's keys—house, bike, and a key she doesn't recognize—left on the bleachers with a folded note: 'Don't tell my parents. Please.' Emotional beat: dread cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The town mobilizes around the 'missing girl' narrative; Priya's parents perform grief while Wendell notices details that don't fit—the packed bag Priya joked about, the deleted group chat. Emotional beat: isolation of knowing something the crowd doesn't.

chapters.title: The Unknown Key
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell tries the mystery key against every lock she can think of and finally opens a bus-station locker containing cash, a burner phone, and a map with three towns circled. Emotional beat: vertigo—Priya planned this, and didn't trust her with it.

chapters.title: Deputy Reyes Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The deputy interviews Wendell, probing the nature of her friendship with Priya; Wendell lies about how close they were, terrified of being outed before she's ready. Emotional beat: the cost of the closet compounding into the cost of the search.

chapters.title: Theater Kids and Other Aliens
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, introducing Marcus, the openly gay senior Wendell has avoided for years. Marcus recognizes what the keys mean before Wendell says it. He becomes her reluctant guide. Emotional beat: first crack in Wendell's armor—being seen without permission.

chapters.title: Coded in Chemistry
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Decoding Priya's notes using their old chemistry shorthand, Wendell finds a message: 'I couldn't be both. You still can. Choose better than me.' Emotional beat: guilt and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Chandrasekarans
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Invited to 'help' the family, Wendell witnesses the suffocating control behind their perfect front—Priya's mother monitoring everything, a college acceptance letter hidden in a drawer. Emotional beat: understanding why Priya ran, and hating that she does.

chapters.title: Marcus's Garage
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus shows Wendell the network of kids across three counties who help runaways—his cousin among them. Wendell must decide whether to trust strangers. Emotional beat: found family offered before she believes she deserves it.

chapters.title: Scholarship Deadline
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The scholarship interview looms; Wendell's mother, a nurse working doubles, frames it as their family's one door out. Wendell realizes Priya's disappearance is costing her the future they planned together. Emotional beat: love against duty, first full collision.

chapters.title: The Burner Rings
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The burner phone rings at 3 a.m.—Priya, breathless, safe, refusing to say where. She asks Wendell to cover for her one more week. Wendell, furious and relieved, says yes. Emotional beat: complicity as intimacy; the closet deepening.

chapters.title: Rumor at the Diner
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. A photo of Priya at a Greyhound stop circulates online; the town's sympathy curdles into suspicion of 'that Chandrasekaran girl' and, by extension, her friends. Wendell's name surfaces. Emotional beat: the town's gaze turning predatory.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finally opens her own locker—her symbol of hiding—and finds Priya's real goodbye letter inside, written before she left: a confession of love, and of fear. Emotional beat: the book's emotional center; grief and love arriving together.

chapters.title: Coming Out in a Parking Lot
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Cornered by rumors, Wendell tells Marcus's circle—and then, accidentally, half the school parking lot—the truth about herself and Priya. Emotional beat: terror, then unexpected lightness; labels coming off.

chapters.title: Her Mother's House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Priya's. Priya's chapter: hiding with the network in a neighboring town, wrestling with guilt over Wendell and terror that her mother will find her. Emotional beat: the runner's side of the story; love as the thing she ran from and toward.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Deputy Reyes reveals she's known where Priya likely is for days—and that she ran away herself at seventeen. She offers Wendell a window before the state search escalates. Emotional beat: an adult ally; duty and mercy shaking hands.

chapters.title: Interview Day
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell gives the scholarship interview while half-listening to a police scanner frequency Marcus rigged, then walks out mid-interview when news breaks that Priya's been spotted and her father is driving to retrieve her. Emotional beat: choosing Priya over the plan, out loud.

chapters.title: Three Towns Over
chapters.summary: Wendell and Marcus's POV, alternating. The road trip: Wendell and Marcus race the Chandrasekarans' car to the depot, Wendell rehearsing what she'll say. Emotional beat: momentum, terror, and the strange joy of being fully herself for the first time.

chapters.title: The Bus Depot
chapters.summary: Wendell and Priya's POV, alternating. Climax: Wendell reaches Priya minutes before her father arrives. Priya is ready to run forever; Wendell offers a third path—come back, but on their terms, with Reyes brokering safety and the network as witness. Priya's father arrives to find them holding hands, unhidden. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: Terms of Return
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The fallout: a mediated family reckoning, Priya staying with Reyes temporarily, the town digesting two out girls at once. Wendell's mother, stunned, chooses her daughter over the neighbors' opinions. Emotional beat: the cost paid, and worth it.

chapters.title: What the Scholarship Was For
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell loses the scholarship but wins a regional award and a mentor through Marcus's network—proof that the exit was never the only door. Priya enrolls in the county school with an emancipation petition pending. Emotional beat: ambition redefined as building, not escaping.

chapters.title: Locker Open
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, final day of junior year. Wendell leaves her own locker open and decorated, a message to the next invisible kid; she and Priya paint the water tower with the network's symbol. Emotional beat: resolution—identity claimed, family found, home chosen instead of fled.
